Jozefow nad Wisla Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Poland

Not demolished. Jews settled in Józefów shortly after the town's founding in 1687, under a privilege granting equal settlement rights to all faiths, and had become the town's largest population group by the 18th century, reaching 85 percent by 1861. WWI and a series of fires devastated the town, reducing it to just 215 inhabitants by 1915; a partial recovery before WWII was cut short when 1,270 Jews were deported to the Sobibór death camp on May 7, 1942. This cemetery, established in the second half of the 17th century with its oldest tombstone dated 1702, received burials up until that same year; it was formally liquidated in 1972 with official consent from Lublin's Voivodeship Monument Conservator, and a garbage dump was later established on part of the site. About 150 tombstones survive today, mostly displaced and broken, alongside rows of tombstone bases marking the original burial layout; local farmers still use the grounds to store grubbed-up fruit tree roots.
